title: Oregon QB Dante Moore sustains concussion after hit by USC's Stephens, no return timetable set
dek: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore suffered a concussion after being hit by USC linebacker Desman Stephens during the second quarter of Saturday's 41-27 win. MRI and CT scans came back clean. Moore will enter concussion protocol with no set timetable for return, and backup Dylan Raiola will lead the offense.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Moore, a projected first-round pick who returned to Oregon despite being widely projected as a top 2026 NFL draft selection, sustained the injury after less than four games and is now facing an uncertain return timeline despite clean imaging.
bottom_line: Moore's return date is undefined pending clearance from concussion protocol. The Ducks' bye week on October 5 provides initial space for evaluation, but whether Moore can return before the regular season ends and whether Raiola's strong performance alters the quarterback hierarchy will shape both Oregon's playoff odds and Moore's draft trajectory.
body:
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore sustained a concussion on Saturday after being hit by USC linebacker Desman Stephens while sliding during the second quarter of the Ducks' 41-27 win. An MRI and CT scans performed immediately after came back clean with no additional injuries, according to Oregon coach Dan Lanning's statement.
Moore was tended to by training staff on the field for an extended period following the hit,  At the hospital, Moore had movement in all his extremities and was being evaluated, per ESPN's reporting. Lanning said: "Dante sustained a concussion in last night's game, but fortunately, his MRI and CT scans came back clean, and he did not suffer any additional injuries. Every concussion is different, and we are going to move forward with an abundance of caution to ensure we make the best decisions for Dante and his future."
Moore will enter concussion protocol with no clear timetable for his return, per CBS Sports. The Ducks enter a bye week before hosting No. 23 UCLA on October 10. Moore had completed 8 of 10 passes early in the game against USC before the injury.
Stephens was penalized for targeting and ejected from the game. While Moore was still on the ground, Stephens ran around the field celebrating the hit and continued to do so with teammates even after being called for targeting and ejected, according to ESPN. USC coach Lincoln Riley announced Sunday that Stephens would be suspended for the Trojans' next game against visiting Washington on October 3 due to his conduct after the incident. Stephens released a statement via the school: "Seeing a player injured like that is incredibly serious, and my reaction in the moments afterward was completely inappropriate and inexcusable. Regardless of what was going through my mind at the time, there is no justification for smiling or celebrating while another player receives medical attention. I take full responsibility for my actions." Riley said in a statement: "Desman's actions in last night's game are unacceptable and are not reflective of USC Football nor of his personal character. He understands his mistake, accepts the consequences of his actions and will learn from this. The entire Trojan Family wishes Dante a full recovery, and we send our best regards to him and his family."
Moore was a preseason Heisman Trophy contender and widely projected as a top pick in the 2026 NFL draft before opting to return to Oregon for his senior year. In four games, he has thrown for 926 passing yards and nine touchdowns while completing 69.7 percent of his passes, per CBS Sports.
Backup quarterback Dylan Raiola entered the game for Moore and led Oregon to victory. Raiola, a former five-star recruit and two-year starter at Nebraska, transferred to Oregon this offseason. He threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns on 11.6 yards per attempt in Moore's absence and is expected to lead the Ducks during Moore's rehabilitation, per CBS Sports.
